text:
Turbidity resulting from construction and clearing activities would adversely affect the water quality of the Thompson River and its tributaries within the proposed reservoir area and about 1.8 miles of stream between the dam site and Lake Jocassee, possibly affecting populations of benthic organisms and fish dependent on such organisms for food. Such effects would be temporary, lasting until the disturbed areas were rehabilitated by seeding of grasses, reforestation, and other measures. The extent of the adverse impacts on stream fauna is not known, nor is the length of time known that would be required for the stream to recover from such impacts.
Stream flow in the 1.8-mile section of Thompson River between the dam site and Lake Jocassee could be limited to seepage from the project dam. Such flow reductions would further reduce the suitability of the stream to support trout. Flow augmentation measures could also adversely affect the trout fishery unless water similar in temperature, dissolved oxygen, and turbidity to that of the Thompson River below the damsite was used for such measures.
A portion of Lake Jocassee at or near its confluence with the Thompson River would experience increases in turbidity following construction activities at the Long Spur Ridge site. Should turbid conditions persist, fish species might migrate to other parts of the lake.
8.3.1.3 Water Quality
Water quality of the Thompson River has been sampled near its confluence with Lake Jocassee (Table 8-6). Data collected at this station should approximate the quality of the water in the vicinity of the Long Spur Ridge alternative site.
Water quality of the Thompson River appears to be very similar in most respects to that of streams in the Howard Creek Basin. Alkalinity and hardness are very low, as is specific conductance, indicating soft, poorly buffered water with a paucity of dissolved solids. Hydrogen ion concentration (pH) fluctuates considerably with a mean value near 6.4. Temperatures range from 3°C to 20°C, while dissolved oxygen values range from 7.9 to 12.0 mg/l. Nutrient levels are low, as are concentrations of metals (not shown in Table 8-6). Turbidity fluctuates, but aside from one high value (124 JTU), recorded values are not greater than 13 JTU. In general, the water quality is good in this stream with purity similar to that of other tributary steams in the area.
